elements.element: No obligation on Customer to disclose more favourable third-party commercial offers to Vendor
elements.evidence: "Customer is not required to disclose ... any more favourable commercial offer it receives"

elements.element: No obligation on Customer to match a more favourable third-party offer for Vendor (right to match / MFN running against Customer)
elements.evidence: "is not required to ... match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer"

elements.element: MFN in Customer's favour permitted but not required (no adverse MFN created)
elements.evidence: Clause imposes no MFN duty on Customer and creates none against Vendor

elements.element: Any MFN limited to a defined product/service
elements.evidence: No MFN obligation survives to be scoped: "is not required to disclose or match"

elements.element: Any MFN limited to a 12-month duration
elements.evidence: No duration term appears in revised 7.2

reasons: The locked preferred level is fully achieved: the single operator flip converts the mandatory disclose-and-match MFN into an express statement that Customer is not required to disclose or match third-party offers.
Both limbs of the original burden (disclosure and matching) are negated by "not required to disclose or match", so neither can be revived independently.
Fallback elements (defined product, 12 months, comparison carve-outs) are inapplicable because no MFN obligation on Customer remains; preferred and fallback are not mixed.
Minimal: only the operative verb phrase in the one offending sentence was changed; no new exceptions, defined terms, or boilerplate were added, and the deterministic minimality gate passes.

Intent preserved: the residual lead-in "Before engaging another provider," is harmless context, no other term is disturbed, and the result is consistent with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer gives no most-favoured-customer commitment.
